stem:
Equal volumes of saturated solutions of magnesium hydroxide, calcium hydroxide and strontium
hydroxide are completely neutralised with dilute sulfuric acid.
The water is gently evaporated from each of the resulting solutions, leaving the corresponding solid
sulfates.
These solid sulfates are completely dissolved in the minimum volume of water needed to produce
saturated solutions.
Which statement about the volumes of water needed to dissolve the sulfates is correct?
The calcium sulfate will require the greatest volume of water.

options.A: The magnesium sulfate will require the greatest volume of water.
options.B: The strontium sulfate will require the greatest volume of water.
options.C: They will all require the same volume of water.

stem: Which statement comparing magnesium and barium, or their compounds, is correct?

options.A: Magnesium reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid more rapidly than barium does.
options.B: One mole of magnesium carbonate gives off a greater amount of gas when it reacts with an excess of dilute hydrochloric acid than one mole of barium carbonate does.
options.C: The solubility of magnesium sulfate in water is greater than the solubility of barium sulfate in water.
options.D: Magnesium carbonate undergoes thermal decomposition less readily than barium carbonate does.
